reading: The report examines whether climate change will bring more frequent disruption to aviation.
Storms near London and across northern Europe caused extensive delays during a busy summer travel period.
Controllers had to guide aircraft around storm cells, reducing the usable airspace.
Congestion consequently left some departures waiting on the ground.
Some planes might need to change their routes.
Diverting to another airport creates additional demands for aircraft parking and passenger facilities.
Pilots have access to weather radar and forecasts, but rapidly moving storms can still require decisions late in a flight.
Longer diversions may increase fuel consumption and add to airlines’ operating costs.
Flooding presents another risk by disrupting airport operations or blocking passengers’ access by road and rail.
These concerns describe potential pressures on the system, rather than a prediction that every flight will be affected.
